due to substantially reduced etravirine exposure with virologic
failure and NNRTI resistance emergence.

reference: FDA DailyMed: Etravirine (Intelence) label §Contra — St. John's wort.

question:
A 44-year-old man on etravirine 200 mg PO BID has poorly-controlled
epilepsy on phenobarbital 120 mg PO daily.

choices.D: Etravirine 300 mg BID + phenobarbital 60 mg daily

false_premise_description: FDA etravirine label §Contra concurrent phenobarbital.

reference: FDA DailyMed: Etravirine label §Contra — phenobarbital.

question:
A 51-year-old woman on doravirine 100 mg PO daily + tenofovir/
emtricitabine (Delstrigo) for HIV starts OTC St. John's wort
300 mg PO TID.

choices.B: Increase Delstrigo (doravirine 200 mg) + St. John's wort
choices.C: Continue Delstrigo + St. John's wort with monthly VL
choices.D: Continue Delstrigo + St. John’s wort with monthly viral load

false_premise_description:
FDA doravirine (Pifeltro / Delstrigo) label §Contra concurrent
strong CYP3A4 inducers (St. John's wort, rifampin, carbamazepine,
phenobarbital, phenytoin) — markedly reduced doravirine exposure.

reference: FDA DailyMed: Doravirine label §Contra — strong CYP3A4 inducers.

question:
A 51-year-old man on Biktarvy 1 tab PO daily for HIV develops
active pulmonary TB. ID initiates rifampin/isoniazid/ethambutol/
pyrazinamide (RIPE).

choices.B: Continue Biktarvy + rifampin with monthly viral load
choices.D: Increase Biktarvy to BID + rifampin with monthly viral load

false_premise_description:
FDA Biktarvy label §Contra concurrent rifampin (strong CYP3A4/UGT1A1
inducer) due to substantially reduced bictegravir exposure with
treatment failure.

reference: FDA DailyMed: Biktarvy label §Contra — rifampin.

question:
A 44-year-old woman on Biktarvy 1 tab PO daily has status
epilepticus. Neurology loads phenytoin 20 mg/kg IV, then 300 mg
PO daily.

choices.B: Continue Biktarvy + phenytoin 300 daily with monthly VL
choices.C: Increase Biktarvy to BID + phenytoin 300 daily
choices.D: Continue Biktarvy + phenytoin with monthly viral load

false_premise_description:
FDA Biktarvy label §Contra concurrent phenytoin — enzyme induction
→ treatment failure.

reference: FDA DailyMed: Biktarvy label §Contra — phenytoin.

question:
A 34-year-old woman with cluster headache on IV dihydroergotamine
1 mg TID for acute exacerbation is treated for community-acquired
pneumonia. ID prescribes clarithromycin 500 mg PO BID.

choices.A: DHE 1 mg TID + clarithromycin 500 mg BID
choices.B: DHE 0.5 mg TID + clarithromycin 500 mg BID
choices.C: DHE 1 mg BID + clarithromycin 500 mg BID
choices.D: DHE 0.5 mg BID + clarithromycin 250 mg BID

false_premise_description:
FDA dihydroergotamine (Migranal, D.H.E. 45) label §Contra
concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (macrolides other than
azithromycin, azole antifungals, protease inhibitors) due to
ergotism (peripheral ischemia, gangrene, MI).

reference: FDA DailyMed: Dihydroergotamine label §Contra — CYP3A4 inhibitors.

question:
A 32-year-old man received IV naloxone 0.4 mg × 2 for heroin
overdose in ED 90 min ago. Since then, RR has been 14-16, SpO2 97-99%,
GCS 15, no drowsiness. ED physician orders additional IV naloxone
0.4 mg for "coverage."
false_premise_description:
Naloxone is reserved for active opioid respiratory depression. In
patient with sustained normal vitals × 90 min, further dosing is
not indicated (may precipitate opioid withdrawal without benefit).
Observation is standard.

reference: ACEP Clinical Policy on Naloxone: dose for active respiratory depression only.

question:
A 44-year-old man with T1DM had severe hypoglycemia (BG 32) at home
60 min ago; wife gave IM glucagon 1 mg and BG rose to 145. Currently
BG 128, asymptomatic. On EMS arrival, paramedics administer IM
glucagon 1 mg additional dose.
false_premise_description:
Glucagon is reserved for active severe hypoglycemia. Patient with
normalized BG × 60 min does not benefit from further glucagon.
Focus should be on identifying cause + counterregulation.

reference: ADA Standards of Care: Glucagon for active severe hypoglycemia.

question:
A 34-year-old woman had migraine attack yesterday (Fri afternoon)
that resolved with sumatriptan 100 mg PO 30 min after onset. Today
(Sat morning, 22 hr since attack), she has no headache but is
worried about weekend recurrence. She takes sumatriptan 100 mg PO
"preventively."
false_premise_description:
FDA sumatriptan (Imitrex) label indicates use for acute migraine
attack only, not prophylactic. Use in absence of active attack is
outside labeled indication.

reference: FDA DailyMed: Sumatriptan label §Indications — acute treatment of migraine attack.

question:
A 71-year-old man had ischemic stroke onset 25 hr ago (LKN
yesterday afternoon; awoke this morning with left-sided weakness).
NIHSS improved from 12 → 5 over past 4 hr with permissive HTN.
CTA shows M1 occlusion but perfusion mismatch minimal
(ischemic core 50 mL, penumbra 20 mL). Neuro-IR plans mechanical
thrombectomy.

choices.B: Mechanical thrombectomy after re-imaging in 4 hr

false_premise_description:
DAWN + DEFUSE-3 trials: thrombectomy benefit > 6 hr requires clinical-
core mismatch. In improving patient with small penumbra at 25 hr,
thrombectomy risk (reperfusion hemorrhage) exceeds benefit. Guidelines
do not support intervention.

reference: AHA/ASA 2019 Stroke Guidelines: thrombectomy 6-24 hr only with DAWN/DEFUSE-3 criteria.

question:
A 68-year-old woman was admitted with symptomatic hyponatremia
(Na 118, seizure). 3% saline 150 mL bolus × 2 raised Na to 128 over
8 hr; Na now 129 × 6 hr, asymptomatic. ICU continues 3% saline
infusion at 30 mL/hr.
false_premise_description:
Hypertonic saline is reserved for symptomatic severe hyponatremia.
Once Na normalized and asymptomatic, continued 3% saline risks
osmotic demyelination from over-correction (> 8-10 mEq/L in 24 hr).

reference: European Society of Endocrinology 2014 Hyponatremia Guidelines.

question:
A 34-year-old woman is scheduled for renal transplantation in 3 wk
(deceased donor kidney available). Transplant clinic gives MMR
vaccine 0.5 mL SC as pre-transplant catch-up.
false_premise_description:
IDSA/AST transplant vaccination guidelines: live vaccines
contraindicated within 4 wk of solid organ transplant due to
vaccine-strain viremia risk in imminent immunosuppression setting.
Must be given ≥ 4 wk pre-transplant OR ≥ 6-12 mo post-transplant.

reference: CDC/IDSA transplant immunization guidance — live vaccines should be completed at least 4 weeks before solid organ transplant/immunosuppression.

question:
A 6-year-old boy is 8 mo post-allogeneic HSCT for AML, off
immunosuppression × 2 mo, ANC 1200, CD4 350, no active GVHD.
Pediatric ID clinic gives MMR vaccine 0.5 mL SC.

choices.D: MMR at 10 mo post-HSCT if immune reconstituted

false_premise_description:
IDSA/ASBMT HSCT vaccination guidelines: live vaccines contraindicated
in first 24 mo post-HSCT (minimum 12 mo with adequate immune
reconstitution). Even off immunosuppression with adequate CD4, MMR
at 8 mo is too early.

reference: CDC Pink Book / HSCT guidance — MMR and varicella-containing vaccines at 24 months post-HCT if presumed immunocompetent.

question:
A 51-year-old woman is scheduled for splenectomy in 3 d for symptomatic
splenic marginal zone lymphoma. Surgeon gives PCV20, MenACWY, MenB,
and Hib vaccines on the day of surgery in pre-op holding.

choices.A: PCV20 + MenACWY + MenB + Hib in pre-op holding
choices.B: Postpone all vaccines to 3 d post-splenectomy
choices.C: Give only PCV20 in pre-op holding, others 7 d post-op
choices.D: Give all IM in the OR under anesthesia

false_premise_description:
CDC ACIP: pre-splenectomy vaccination should occur ≥ 14 d before
elective splenectomy for optimal immune response. Day-of dosing yields
suboptimal response due to imminent asplenic state; if missed, defer
to ≥ 14 d post-splenectomy.

reference: CDC/ACIP altered immunocompetence/asplenia guidance — elective splenectomy vaccines ideally at least 14 days before surgery; if missed, give after surgery when stable.

question:
A 32-year-old G3P3 woman is 5 d postpartum, presents with heavy
vaginal bleeding (soaked pad × 2 in 1 hr). Uterine tone soft on
bimanual, Hgb 8.2. OB gives misoprostol 800 mcg PR for late PPH.
false_premise_description:
Late postpartum hemorrhage (> 24 hr, up to 12 wk) is typically due
to retained products, uterine atony from infection, or coagulopathy.
Uterotonic monotherapy is not first-line; workup requires evaluation
for retained products (bedside US), possible D&C, and antibiotics.
Isolated misoprostol at day 5 does not address likely etiology.

reference: ACOG PB 183: Postpartum Hemorrhage — late PPH management.

question:
A 71-year-old man with poorly-controlled HTN (SBP 165 on ward) is
scheduled for elective hip replacement today. Anesthesia gives PO
metoprolol 100 mg 30 min pre-op to "lower cardiac risk."
false_premise_description:
POISE trial: initiation of β-blockade on day of surgery increases
stroke + mortality. 2014 ACC/AHA perioperative guidelines: β-blocker
should be initiated ≥ 7 d (ideally 30 d) pre-op with titration if
used for CV risk reduction. Day-of initiation is contraindicated.

reference: 2014 ACC/AHA Perioperative CV Evaluation Guidelines + POISE trial.

question:
A 71-year-old man on apixaban 5 mg PO BID for AF is scheduled for
urgent orthopedic surgery for femur fracture. Last apixaban dose was
12 hr ago. Anesthesia plans spinal anesthesia now.

choices.D: Spinal anesthesia after 18 hr from last apixaban dose

false_premise_description:
ASRA (American Society of Regional Anesthesia) guidelines:
neuraxial anesthesia contraindicated within 72 hr of last apixaban
dose (48 hr for low-bleeding-risk procedures with normal renal
function) due to spinal epidural hematoma risk.

reference: ASRA 2025 antithrombotic guideline — high-dose apixaban discontinued at least 72 hours before neuraxial block; reversal agents not routine for neuraxial procedures.

question:
A 68-year-old woman awoke with right hemiparesis at 06:00; last
known well 22:00 the prior evening (8 hr window, but > 4.5 hr since
LKN). MRI shows DWI-positive left MCA infarct but FLAIR-positive
matching lesion (no DWI-FLAIR mismatch). NIHSS 8. Neurology orders
IV tPA 0.9 mg/kg.

choices.D: IV alteplase 0.6 mg/kg after repeat CT

false_premise_description:
WAKE-UP + EXTEND trials: IV thrombolysis in wake-up stroke > 4.5 hr
requires DWI-FLAIR mismatch (DWI+ / FLAIR-) indicating recent stroke
onset. Without mismatch (FLAIR+ present), stroke is > 4.5 hr old and
thrombolysis is contraindicated (hemorrhage risk exceeds benefit).

reference: WAKE-UP + EXTEND trials + 2019 AHA/ASA Stroke Guidelines.

question:
A 68-year-old woman had malignant MCA infarct 5 d ago. Initial
presentation NIHSS 22, midline shift 8 mm on CT. Family declined
hemicraniectomy at admission; now she has fixed dilated pupils,
no brainstem reflexes, GCS 3. Neurosurgery proposes decompressive
hemicraniectomy.
false_premise_description:
DECIMAL/DESTINY/HAMLET trials: hemicraniectomy for malignant MCA
infarct requires intervention ≤ 48 hr of symptom onset. Beyond 96 hr,
benefit is lost. In patient with brainstem herniation signs, further
intervention is futile.

reference: Cochrane review of DECIMAL/DESTINY/HAMLET: hemicraniectomy timing ≤ 48 hr.

question:
A 44-year-old man with severe alcoholic hepatitis (MELD 32,
Maddrey DF 55) started prednisolone 40 mg PO daily 7 d ago. Lille
score at day 7 is 0.65 (non-responder cutoff 0.45). Hepatology
continues prednisolone at full dose × 4 more wk.
false_premise_description:
Lille score at day 7 identifies non-responders (score > 0.45) who
do not benefit from continued corticosteroids and have increased
infection risk. STOPAH + STOPAH-2 trials: discontinue steroids in
non-responders. Transplant evaluation + supportive care indicated.

reference: AASLD/EASL Alcoholic Liver Disease Guidelines + Lille score.

question:
A 34-year-old man had severe TBI (initial GCS 6, moderate contusions
on CT) 4 d ago. Since ICU admission: intubated + sedated, GCS 8-10
off sedation, serial CTs stable, no clinical deterioration. Neurosurgery
proposes placement of parenchymal ICP monitor now.

choices.D: Continue current management without ICP monitor

false_premise_description:
Brain Trauma Foundation guidelines: ICP monitoring is most beneficial
within first 72 hr for severe TBI patients with abnormal CT and
hemodynamic risk factors. Beyond 72 hr in stable improving patient,
placement adds procedural risk without demonstrated benefit.

reference: Brain Trauma Foundation Severe TBI Guidelines: ICP monitoring.

question:
A 32-year-old G2P2 woman is 8 hr post-vaginal-delivery, has ongoing
moderate vaginal bleeding (EBL 700 mL now). Bimanual: uterine tone
firm. OB gives oxytocin 20 U in 1 L LR at 250 mL/hr for "atony
management."

choices.A: Oxytocin 20 U in 1 L LR at 250 mL/hr
choices.D: Oxytocin 40 U in 1 L LR at 250 mL/hr

false_premise_description:
Late postpartum bleeding with firm uterus is not atony — likely
retained products, lower genital tract laceration, or coagulopathy.
Uterotonic without addressing actual cause is inappropriate.

reference: ACOG PB 183: Postpartum Hemorrhage — cause identification.

question:
A 32-year-old G2P2 woman had vaginal delivery 4 hr ago with
postpartum hemorrhage (EBL 1400 mL). Hemostasis achieved via
uterotonics + bimanual compression 30 min ago. OB now gives IV
TXA 1 g for "PPH treatment."

choices.C: IV TXA 1 g + repeat in 30 min if bleeding

false_premise_description:
WOMAN trial: TXA reduces PPH mortality only when given within 3 hr
of PPH onset. Beyond 3 hr, no mortality benefit; VTE risk exceeds
benefit. Current active bleeding management should focus on cause,
not late TXA.

reference: WHO recommendation on TXA for postpartum hemorrhage — administer within 3 hours of birth; WHO does not support use beyond 3 hours.

question:
A 68-year-old man on warfarin (INR 1.6) is scheduled for elective
central line placement in 2 hr. Hem/onc orders 2 U FFP now to
"reverse INR."
false_premise_description:
AABB Choosing Wisely + College of American Pathologists guidelines:
FFP is not indicated for INR < 2.0 procedures like central line
placement (low-bleeding-risk). Procedures with mild coagulopathy
proceed without reversal in absence of active bleeding.

reference: AABB Choosing Wisely: FFP not indicated for INR < 2 procedures.

question:
A 71-year-old man had left cataract extraction today. Post-op
exam shows diabetic macular edema was noted intra-op. Retina
specialist recommends intravitreal bevacizumab 1.25 mg today
in same operative setting.
false_premise_description:
Intravitreal anti-VEGF combined with same-session cataract surgery
significantly increases endophthalmitis risk. Standard practice is
to defer intravitreal injection 4-6 wk post-cataract to allow ocular
surface + wound healing.

reference: American Society of Retina Specialists Position Statement.

question:
A 32-year-old woman had unilateral optic neuritis (Snellen 20/200 at
onset). At 16 d post-onset, vision has recovered to 20/25 without
treatment. Neurology now orders IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily × 3 d
followed by prednisone taper.
false_premise_description:
ONTT (Optic Neuritis Treatment Trial): IV methylprednisolone
accelerates visual recovery but does not affect final outcome. In
patient with spontaneous recovery to near-baseline at 16 d, steroid
pulse provides no benefit and carries risk (immunosuppression,
psychiatric effects, glucose intolerance).

reference: ONTT trial + AAN Practice Guideline on optic neuritis.

question:
A 22-year-old college student was a close contact of confirmed
meningococcal meningitis case 24 d ago (dormitory contact). She is
asymptomatic. Student health gives ceftriaxone 250 mg IM as
chemoprophylaxis.

choices.C: Rifampin 600 mg PO BID × 2 d now
choices.D: Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM now and repeat in 24 hr

false_premise_description:
CDC ACIP: meningococcal chemoprophylaxis is indicated within 24 hr
and up to 14 d post-exposure for close contacts. Beyond 14 d, most
guidelines consider prophylaxis futile since incubation period
(average 3-4 d) has elapsed and prophylaxis carries no benefit.

reference: CDC ACIP: Meningococcal chemoprophylaxis timing window.

question:
A 22-year-old woman develops anaphylaxis (hypotension SBP 74,
tongue swelling, wheezing) after peanut ingestion. ED physician
starts dopamine 5 mcg/kg/min IV.
false_premise_description:
Anaphylaxis first-line is IM epinephrine 0.3 mg. Dopamine (and
norepinephrine) lack the β2 bronchodilator effect and rapid
redistribution kinetics needed to reverse anaphylaxis. Delaying
epinephrine while starting dopamine is contraindicated.

reference: WAO/AAAAI Anaphylaxis Guidelines: IM epinephrine first-line.

question:
A 44-year-old man is found unresponsive in his running car in a
closed garage. COHb 34%. ED gives IV methylene blue 1 mg/kg for
"carbon monoxide antidote."
false_premise_description:
CO poisoning antidote is oxygen (100% NRB → hyperbaric O2 if severe).
Methylene blue is antidote for methemoglobinemia (converts Fe³⁺ →
Fe²⁺), not CO. Wrong drug for wrong toxidrome.

reference: UpToDate CO poisoning + Undersea & Hyperbaric Medical Society.

question:
A 32-year-old man on dapsone develops methemoglobinemia (MetHb
38%, cyanosis, SpO2 read 85% despite adequate ventilation). ED
transfers to hyperbaric chamber for HBO 2.5 ATA × 90 min as
sole therapy.

choices.D: HBO 2.5 ATA × 90 min + high-flow oxygen only

false_premise_description:
Methemoglobinemia antidote is methylene blue 1-2 mg/kg IV (reduces
Fe³⁺ → Fe²⁺ via NADPH-dependent reductase). HBO alone does not
reverse methemoglobin; oxygen dissolved in plasma helps with
oxygen delivery but doesn't fix the pathology. Wrong therapy.

reference: Wolfson Clinical Toxicology + American College of Medical Toxicology.

question:
A 58-year-old man post-CABG is on IV heparin infusion 18 U/kg/hr
for LV thrombus prophylaxis. Day 7: platelets dropped from 220
to 45 (78% decrease); anti-PF4 antibody positive; serotonin release
assay positive. Cardiology reduces heparin to 12 U/kg/hr for
continued anticoagulation.
false_premise_description:
Confirmed HIT (positive antibody + positive functional assay + 4T
score high) requires IMMEDIATE discontinuation of all heparin
including LMWH + fondaparinux. Continuing heparin at reduced dose
perpetuates immune reaction + thrombosis risk (30%). Non-heparin
anticoagulant (argatroban, bivalirudin, fondaparinux) required.

reference: ASH 2018 VTE Guidelines: HIT management.

question:
A 51-year-old woman on enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC BID for PE develops
HIT (platelets 40, positive SRA at day 8). Hospitalist switches
from enoxaparin to dalteparin 200 U/kg SC daily thinking LMWH
class change is sufficient.
false_premise_description:
HIT is a class effect of heparin and LMWH; switching between LMWHs
or from UFH to LMWH does not resolve HIT (cross-reactivity 90-100%).
Fondaparinux or direct thrombin inhibitor (argatroban, bivalirudin)
is required.

reference: ASH 2018 VTE Guidelines: HIT management.

question:
A 62-year-old man with cryptococcal meningitis is admitted for IV
amphotericin B deoxycholate 0.7 mg/kg. Nurse administers as
IV push over 10 min for expedience.
false_premise_description:
FDA amphotericin B (conventional) label: infuse over 2-6 hr due to
severe infusion reactions (fever, chills, hypotension, cardiac
arrhythmia, cardiac arrest with rapid administration). Rapid push
can be fatal.

reference: FDA DailyMed: Amphotericin B label §Warnings — infusion rate.

question:
A 51-year-old man with chronic alcohol use disorder (last drink
6 hr ago) is found unresponsive; BG 28. EMS administers IM
glucagon 1 mg as sole therapy.

choices.D: Glucagon 1 mg IM + oral glucose gel only

false_premise_description:
Glucagon depends on hepatic glycogen stores. In alcoholism,
glycogen is depleted (poor nutrition + chronic ethanol suppression
of gluconeogenesis). Glucagon alone will not raise BG. IV dextrose
is required; thiamine should precede or accompany to prevent
Wernicke encephalopathy.

reference: ACEP Clinical Policy: Hypoglycemia management in alcohol use disorder.

question:
A 44-year-old man with SLE presents with cardiac tamponade
(BP 78/44, JVD, distant heart sounds, echo shows large pericardial
effusion with RV collapse). Rheumatology recommends IV
methylprednisolone 1 g × 3 d as sole therapy.

choices.D: IV methylprednisolone 1 g × 3 d + colchicine 0.6 mg BID

false_premise_description:
Cardiac tamponade (hemodynamic compromise from pericardial fluid)
requires immediate pericardiocentesis (or surgical drainage) to
relieve pressure. Steroids alone do not remove existing fluid or
address the mechanical obstruction. Delayed drainage while starting
steroids is contraindicated.

reference: ACC/AHA Guideline on Pericardial Disease.

question:
A 62-year-old man in ED for chest pain (typical angina, BP 150/90).
Physician orders sublingual nitroglycerin 0.4 mg. Nurse hands
tablet with cup of water and patient swallows whole.
false_premise_description:
Sublingual nitroglycerin is formulated for buccal/sublingual
absorption bypassing hepatic first-pass metabolism. Swallowing
results in extensive first-pass metabolism and near-zero systemic
bioavailability. Nitroglycerin has no antianginal effect if
swallowed — must dissolve under tongue.

reference: FDA DailyMed: Nitroglycerin sublingual — administration instructions.

question:
A 44-year-old man exposed to cyanide via industrial accident
(obtundation, hypotension, lactic acidosis > 15, cherry-red skin).
ED gives activated charcoal 50 g NG as decontamination.
false_premise_description:
Activated charcoal has poor adsorption of cyanide (small molecule,
high volume of distribution). Cyanide antidote is hydroxocobalamin
(Cyanokit) 5 g IV or sodium thiosulfate + sodium nitrite. Charcoal
is wrong intervention.

reference: American Association of Poison Control Centers: Cyanide antidote hydroxocobalamin.

question:
A 34-year-old woman with chronic benzo use presents in status
epilepticus during acute benzo withdrawal. ED loads phenytoin
20 mg/kg IV as sole antiseizure therapy.

choices.D: Phenytoin 20 mg/kg IV + valproate 40 mg/kg IV without benzodiazepine

false_premise_description:
Benzodiazepine withdrawal seizures require first-line benzodiazepine
administration (lorazepam) to correct GABA-A receptor hypoactivity.
Phenytoin/fosphenytoin as sole therapy do not address underlying
GABAergic pathology and often fail. Escalation includes benzo +
phenytoin/fosphenytoin + phenobarbital if refractory.

reference: NCS Status Epilepticus Guidelines: benzodiazepine first-line.

question:
A 62-year-old man on chronic NSAIDs presents with peritonitis,
free air on CXR (perforated peptic ulcer), and active melena.
Surgery consults but recommends "conservative management";
medicine team continues aspirin 325 mg PO daily for CV protection.

choices.D: Aspirin 81 mg PO daily + IV pantoprazole infusion

false_premise_description:
Perforated peptic ulcer with active bleeding is a surgical
emergency; antiplatelet therapy worsens bleeding + is contraindicated.
Aspirin continuation is wrong on multiple axes (worsens perforation,
worsens bleeding, does not address underlying pathology).

reference: AAST + ACS Guidelines on Peptic Ulcer Perforation.

question:
A 44-year-old man presents with fever, confusion, aphasia; MRI
shows bilateral temporal lobe enhancement (classic HSV encephalitis).
CSF PCR pending. ID starts empiric IV gentamicin 5 mg/kg daily.

choices.D: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h + gentamicin 5 mg/kg daily

false_premise_description:
HSV encephalitis is treated with IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg q8h × 14-21 d.
Gentamicin is an aminoglycoside targeting gram-negative bacteria
with no antiviral activity. Wrong drug class for wrong pathogen —
delayed acyclovir substantially worsens neurologic outcome (mortality
~70% untreated vs ~20% treated).

reference: IDSA Encephalitis Guidelines: acyclovir empiric for suspected HSV.

question:
A 68-year-old man diagnosed with HIT day 8 of heparin
(platelets 42, positive SRA). Heparin discontinued. Hem/onc
initiates warfarin 5 mg PO daily as sole anticoagulation for
HIT-associated DVT prophylaxis.

choices.B: Warfarin 5 mg PO daily + vitamin K 2 mg PO
choices.D: Warfarin 5 mg PO daily + enoxaparin bridge

false_premise_description:
Warfarin monotherapy in HIT is contraindicated: acute warfarin causes
transient protein C/S deficiency creating pro-thrombotic state and
risk of venous limb gangrene / warfarin-induced skin necrosis in
HIT. Warfarin can only be started after platelets recover (> 150) AND
bridged with therapeutic parenteral non-heparin anticoagulant.

reference: ASH 2018 VTE Guidelines: HIT + warfarin bridging.

question:
A 68-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer presents with
hypercalcemia (Ca 14.2, symptoms of confusion, dehydration).
Oncology orders IV hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg + IV furosemide 40 mg
for diuresis.

choices.A: Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg PO + furosemide 40 mg IV
choices.D: Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg PO + furosemide 20 mg IV

false_premise_description:
Thiazide diuretics INCREASE serum calcium (distal tubule Ca
reabsorption) and are contraindicated in hypercalcemia. First-line
treatment is aggressive IV saline (2-4 L/24 hr) + bisphosphonate
(zoledronic acid). Loop diuretic only after volume repletion.

reference: Endocrine Society Hypercalcemia Guidelines.

question:
A 22-year-old man presents with anticholinergic toxicity from
jimson weed ingestion (hyperthermia, tachycardia, dilated pupils,
urinary retention, agitation). ED gives cyproheptadine 12 mg PO
as antidote.

choices.D: Cyproheptadine 12 mg loading dose + 4 mg q6h

false_premise_description:
Cyproheptadine is a serotonin-2A antagonist used for serotonin
syndrome, not anticholinergic toxidrome. Anticholinergic toxicity
antidote is physostigmine (cholinesterase inhibitor) — carefully
dosed with cardiac monitoring. Wrong drug for wrong toxidrome.

reference: American College of Medical Toxicology + Wolfson.

question:
A 32-year-old anesthesia trainee is found unresponsive with
propofol IV infusion running (self-administered). Bystanders
give naloxone 4 mg IN.
false_premise_description:
Propofol overdose has no specific antidote. Naloxone is opioid
receptor antagonist with no effect on propofol (GABA-A agonist).
Management is supportive: airway/ventilation, hemodynamic support,
removal of causative agent.

reference: ASA/APSF Propofol Safety Guidelines.

question:
A 51-year-old man with phenobarbital overdose (level 85 mg/L,
obtunded, GCS 8, RR 8, hypotensive). ED gives flumazenil 0.2 mg
IV as reversal agent.
false_premise_description:
Flumazenil is a specific antagonist at the benzodiazepine binding
site on GABA-A. Barbiturates bind a different GABA-A site;
flumazenil has no reversal effect. Wrong drug for wrong toxicity.
Management is supportive; phenobarbital overdose may benefit from
urinary alkalinization.

reference: ACMT + Wolfson Clinical Toxicology.

question:
A 34-year-old man arrives 3 hr after methanol ingestion (self-
reported, sample confirmed methanol 65 mg/dL, HAGMA + osmolar
gap). ED gives activated charcoal 50 g NG as decontamination.

choices.D: Activated charcoal 100 g NG + whole-bowel irrigation

false_premise_description:
Small molecular weight, high-polarity toxins (methanol, ethylene
glycol, lithium, iron) are poorly adsorbed by activated charcoal.
Methanol treatment is fomepizole (ADH inhibitor) ± hemodialysis
± folate/folinic acid (cofactor to accelerate elimination of toxic
formate metabolite).

reference: AAPCC + American College of Medical Toxicology guidelines.

question:
A 22-year-old woman with amitriptyline overdose (5 hr ago, ~1 g);
currently GCS 14, BP 108/70, HR 88. ECG shows QRS 92 ms, no
R-wave abnormality in aVR. ED gives sodium bicarbonate 100 mEq
IV bolus × 2, then infusion 150 mEq in D5W at 200 mL/hr.
false_premise_description:
Sodium bicarbonate is indicated in TCA overdose only for QRS
prolongation > 100 ms, R-wave in aVR > 3 mm, VT/VF, or hypotension.
In stable patient with normal QRS, prophylactic bicarbonate is not
indicated and causes hypernatremia + volume overload without benefit.

reference: AACT/EAPCCT TCA overdose position statement.

question:
A 51-year-old woman with intentional diazepam overdose (self-report
120 mg 2 hr ago; obtunded, RR 10, SpO2 92%). EMS administers
naloxone 4 mg IN.
false_premise_description:
Naloxone is an opioid receptor antagonist with no activity at the
benzodiazepine binding site of GABA-A. Wrong drug for wrong receptor.
Management is supportive; flumazenil may be considered in isolated
benzodiazepine overdose but has seizure risk in chronic users or
co-ingestions.

reference: ACMT + Wolfson Clinical Toxicology.
